_meta.indication: REZUROCK is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with chronic graft-versus-host disease (chronic GVHD) after failure of at least two prior lines of systemic therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, multicenter dose-ranging study; patients randomized 1:1 to belumosudil 200 mg daily or 200 mg twice daily, stratified by prior ibrutinib and presence of severe cGVHD.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with chronic GVHD who had failed two to five prior lines of systemic therapy and required additional treatment; median age 53 years, 65% male, 83% Caucasian, median of 3 prior lines of therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary objective: overall response rate (ORR), including complete or partial response (CR or PR) per 2014 NIH consensus criteria; efficacy determined by ORR through Cycle 7 Day 1.
pivotal_trials.n: 132 patients randomized (66 per arm); 65 patients treated on the belumosudil 200 mg once daily arm.
pivotal_trials.result: FDA-adjudicated ORR through Cycle 7 Day 1 was 75% (95% CI: 63, 85) in the 200 mg once daily arm; CR rate was 6% (95% CI 2%, 15%); median duration of response 1.9 months (95% CI: 1.2, 2.9); 62% (95% CI: 46, 74) alive without new systemic therapy for at least 12 months since response.

key_safety: Most common (≥20%) adverse reactions were infections, asthenia, nausea, diarrhea, dyspnea, cough, edema, hemorrhage, abdominal pain, musculoskeletal pain, headache, and hypertension; infection occurred in 53% (16% Grade 3-4), asthenia 46%, nausea 42%, diarrhea 35%. A fatal adverse reaction occurred in one patient; permanent discontinuation for adverse reactions occurred in 18%.
target_moa: Belumosudil is a Rho-associated, coiled-coil containing protein kinase-2 (ROCK2) inhibitor with selective inhibitory activity for ROCK2, downregulating pro-inflammatory (Th17) responses and fibrotic pathways.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not discussed by an Advisory Committee.

summary.text: NDA 214783 for belumosudil, a new molecular entity, was submitted under the 505(b)(1) pathway and received Priority review. It had Orphan Drug Designation (granted October 5, 2017) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation for treatment of adult patients with chronic GVHD after failure of two or more lines of systemic therapy. It was approved by traditional (non-accelerated) approval based on the ORR results of Study KD025-213.
